Study_Title: Cryptographically verifiable authorization for autonomous AI agents: a falsifiable hypothesis and proof of concept
Threat_Attacker_Model: Unauthorised or out-of-scope agent principal attempting to invoke protected tools, replay stale authorization proofs, or leak private policy attributes at the pre-execution gateway; compromised gateway state affects replay freshness.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Groth16 zk-SNARK (Circom/snarkjs, 531 constraints, 537 wires), two-input Poseidon hash for principal commitment, SHA-256 request/plan commitment, and stateful gateway nonce freshness check.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Pre-execution Authorization Verifier Gateway
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Authorization soundness, principal binding, request/policy binding, and attribute privacy under Groth16 knowledge-soundness and hash collision resistance (Equations 27–31, 45–47); replay resistance additionally requires gateway state integrity.
Trust_Assumptions: Groth16 knowledge-soundness and trusted setup ceremony; collision resistance of Poseidon and SHA-256; honest verifier gateway maintaining stateful nonce freshness set N; faithful circuit encoding of relation R_CVA.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: PDF p. 11 Table 3 (n=20 runs, CLI WASM prover on AMD Ryzen 7 7700): witness generation 61.9 ± 1.1 ms, proof generation 351.9 ± 26.6 ms, verification time 309.4 ± 22.6 ms (includes Node.js CLI startup overhead), proof size 805 bytes (531 constraints).
Exposed_Security_Function: Groth16 zero-knowledge proof generation and pre-execution gateway verification (VerifyAuth)
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Table 2 (p. 11) explicitly notes that explicit policy ID public input, context commitment (h_c), and runtime execution binding remain open/unimplemented in the PoC; CLI verification latency (309.4 ms) is dominated by Node.js process startup; Groth16 requires a trusted setup and is not post-quantum secure.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: PARAFRASA dan kutipan metrik terukur. PDF p. 5 Section 3.3 (R_CVA relation); pp. 6–8 Sections 4.1–4.4 (Equations 27–31, 45–47); p. 11 Tables 2–3 (PoC status & n=20 timings: witness 61.9±1.1 ms, prove 351.9±26.6 ms, verify 309.4±22.6 ms, 805 bytes); p. 10 Section 5.6 (trusted setup & post-quantum limitation).
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Parafrasa penulis: Otorisasi agen otonom diformalkan sebagai relasi terverifikasi kriptografis R_CVA menggunakan zk-SNARK Groth16 (531 constraint) yang mengikat identitas prinsipal (Poseidon), komitmen rencana aksi (SHA-256), dan kepuasan kebijakan tanpa mengungkap atribut privat.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Dievaluasi pada model formal kandidat (Section 4) dan purwarupa sirkuit Circom/snarkjs 531-constraint (n=20 run CLI); pengikatan konteks (h_c) dan eksekusi runtime belum diimplementasikan.
Protected_Object: Private agent authorization attributes, principal commitment, and plan-level action request commitment
Composition_Evidence: Menggabungkan komitmen identitas Poseidon, komitmen request SHA-256, bukti Groth16, dan pemeriksaan nonce stateful di gateway, tetapi pengikatan ke eksekusi runtime aktual dinyatakan terbuka (Table 2, p. 11).
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi & Verifikasi Reviewer 2: Studi memenuhi Stream M pada batas B2;B3 melalui reduksi teoretis kandidat (Equations 45–47) dan purwarupa Groth16 (Table 3, p. 11). Kode AD diberikan karena ketergantungan pada trusted setup Groth16, integritas state nonce gateway (epsilon_gateway pada Eq. 47), serta belum diimplementasikannya context binding dan runtime execution binding (Table 2). Penulis secara eksplisit mencatat kerentanan Groth16 terhadap kuantum dan menyarankan alternatif transparan/PQC (STARKs) sebagai arah riset (STAGE_1_SUGGESTED_MIGRATION).
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi silang Reviewer 1 pada REVIEW_AUDIT atas batas reduksi Equations 45–47 dan pencatatan metrik Table 3 (n=20) pada sheet EVALUASI_EMPIRIS_OVERHEAD_RQ3.

Study_Title: NovaFabric: Tamper-Evident, Replayable Evidence for Autonomous AI Agent Runs
Threat_Attacker_Model: Post-hoc trace tampering (field modification, seal removal, timestamp manipulation), capsule deletion/reordering by a dishonest log operator, and accidental secret leakage in shared audit bundles; capture hooks and host proxy are assumed trusted.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Two-tier NovaSeal: Ed25519 detached batch signature at ingestion (did:key), DSSE envelope with ECDSA P-256 over RFC 8785 canonical JSON, RFC 3161 trusted timestamp, append-only Merkle Mountain Range log, and SHA-256 redaction attestation.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Runtime Capture Hooks / Proxy Collector and Offline Capsule/Bundle Verifier
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Tamper-evident integrity and ordering of logged Run Capsules across 15 entity types (100% detection across field modification, seal removal, and timestamp tampering in Table 7), plus deterministic mocked-mode replay without live model calls (10/10 scenarios).
Trust_Assumptions: Capture hooks and local proxy are uncompromised and faithfully record events (Section 3.1 TCB); signing keys (Ed25519/ECDSA P-256) and RFC 3161 TSA are uncompromised; Merkle checkpoints are retained and monitored by witnesses.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: PDF pp. 26–27 Sections 4.4–4.5 & Table 7: 100% tamper detection across 3 mutation classes; mean capsule footprint 76 KB (range 60–88 KB); wall-clock capture overhead median -1.8%, mean +3.2% (n=100 paired runs across 10 scenarios).
Exposed_Security_Function: Ed25519 batch signing, DSSE ECDSA P-256 capsule sealing, RFC 3161 timestamp verification, and Merkle inclusion/consistency proof verification
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Capture is part of the TCB (a compromised host/key custodian can omit events or sign false capsules); full mocked-replay workload completion succeeded in only 2/10 scenarios due to non-model network dependencies (p. 27); Table 5 (p. 25) documents 6 surfaced defects including open defect D5 (forensic mode overclaiming model_calls_mocked) and unreleased defect D6.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: PARAFRASA dan kutipan metrik terukur. PDF p. 11 Section 3.1 (TCB); pp. 14–16 Section 3.5 & Figure 4 (NovaSeal Ed25519 + DSSE ECDSA P-256 + RFC 3161 + Merkle log & ML-DSA migration note); p. 25 Table 5 (defects D1–D6); pp. 26–27 Sections 4.3–4.5 (10/10 no live call, 2/10 full completion, 100% tamper detection, mean +3.2% / median -1.8% capture overhead, 76 KB capsule).
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Parafrasa penulis: NovaFabric merekam jalannya agen ke dalam Run Capsule 15-entitas dan menyegelnya dengan tanda tangan Ed25519, amplop DSSE ECDSA P-256, stempel waktu RFC 3161, log Merkle append-only, dan atestasi redaksi untuk verifikasi pihak ketiga dan replay empat mode.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Dievaluasi pada 10 skenario agen (n=100 run berpasangan), pengujian mutasi kapsul 3 kelas, dan kueri graf provenance 1M–100M edge; jalur verifikasi pihak ketiga tanpa instalasi NovaFabric baru dispesifikasikan dan belum diuji pihak independen.
Protected_Object: 15-entity Run Capsule, Evidence Bundle, Merkle provenance log, and redacted secret attestations
Composition_Evidence: Menyusun rantai bukti berlapis pada B4 (Ed25519 -> DSSE ECDSA P-256 -> RFC 3161 -> Merkle Mountain Range), namun penulis secara eksplisit menyatakan capture hooks berada di dalam TCB dan tidak membuktikan kelengkapan tangkapan terhadap host yang dikompromikan.
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi & Verifikasi Reviewer 2: Studi memenuhi Stream M_AND_A pada B4. Kode DG;AD diberikan karena penulis secara transparan melaporkan kegagalan penyelesaian beban kerja replay penuh pada 8/10 skenario serta cacat implementasi D1–D6 pada Table 5 (DG), dan seluruh jaminan integritas bergantung pada asumsi bahwa hook penangkap di host agen jujur serta kunci penanda tangan tidak bocor (AD). Halaman 15 menyebut secara eksplisit rencana migrasi tanda tangan kapsul dari Ed25519 ke ML-DSA (STAGE_1_SUGGESTED_MIGRATION).
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi silang Reviewer 1 pada REVIEW_AUDIT dan pencatatan observasi overhead (+3.2% mean, -1.8% median, 76 KB) pada sheet EVALUASI_EMPIRIS_OVERHEAD_RQ3.

Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NovaFabric capsule REST ingest and evidence capture; independent defect census.

Exposed_Security_Function: Evidence capture and persistence validation.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: The repair/evaluation fleet was decommissioned. Required-stream coverage and per-call capture recall use different denominators.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: PARAPHRASE; PDF p.25 Table 5 D6; pp.27-28 Section 4.5; pp.33-36 Sections 4.10-4.11.
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Parafrasa sumber: The evaluation exposed an ingest path acknowledging 41774 uploads while writing no metadata rows; repair was in main, unreleased and not revalidated on the original fleet.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Reported D6 historical build and campaign; does not establish the defect remains in every current release.
Protected_Object: Acknowledged capsule metadata and required evidence streams.
Composition_Evidence: Signing/log integrity cannot guarantee capture or persistence of never-recorded events.

Study_Title: NiyamAI - An Intent-Bound AI Agent with Cryptographically Verifiable Guardrails using Zero-Knowledge Proofs
Threat_Attacker_Model: Prompt injection, goal hijacking, tool-argument manipulation, and host-local guardrail bypass where an untrusted agent host claims a safety policy was evaluated without verifiable execution evidence.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: SHA-256 Intent Contract commitment (IntentHash); deterministic authority gate; neural Judge (11->8->2 MLP in PyTorch/ONNX); EZKL circuit (431 rows at logrows=15) with Halo2KZG zkSNARK proof generation and verification.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Pre-tool execution interception gate, neural Judge evaluator, and Halo2KZG proof verifier
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Theorem 1 (p. 5 §3.5) provides a proof sketch of execution-control soundness for Judge computation J(x,w) conditioned on SHA-256 collision resistance and Halo2KZG knowledge soundness; across 2,000 AgentSafetyBench scenarios, achieves 88.8% F1 at 1.0% FPR (99.6% unsafe-action blocking in end-to-end simulation).
Trust_Assumptions: Faithful input/feature extraction and Intent Contract binding; trusted enforcement gate and verifier path; SHA-256 collision resistance and Halo2KZG knowledge soundness (local SRS generated for testing; production requires trusted setup).
Performance_Overhead_Reported: PDF p. 9 Table III & p. 10 Table V (n=30, CPU): witness generation 27.6 ± 5.9 ms; proof generation mean 1,694.5 ± 92.0 ms (median 1,722.04 ms, p95 1,688.96 ms—internal table inversion noted); proof verification 50.7 ± 7.5 ms; pre-ZK gate+Judge latency <1 ms; full pipeline mean 1,582.8 ± 512.9 ms per tool call; proof size 18.64 ± 0.04 KB (text p. 1 states 18.6 KB / p. 9 states 18.68 KB).
Exposed_Security_Function: SHA-256 Intent Contract commitment and Halo2KZG zero-knowledge proof verification
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Halo2KZG proof certifies that the 11->8->2 MLP Judge executed on the extracted 11-feature vector, not that feature extraction or semantic user intent alignment is unbypassable (content moderation category recall drops compared to 97.6–99.6% on structural categories, p. 11); Table III p. 9 exhibits an internal statistical inversion (reported p95 1,688.96 ms < median 1,722.04 ms) and minor proof-size discrepancy (18.64 KB vs 18.68 KB); ~1.7 s proving latency per allowed tool call.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: PARAFRASA dan audit langsung PDF ter-pin. PDF p. 1 Abstract (2,000 AgentSafetyBench scenarios, 88.8% F1, 1.0% FPR); pp. 4–6 Sections 3.3–3.8 & Theorem 1 (SHA-256 IntentHash, Halo2KZG); p. 9 Table III (proving 1,694.5±92.0 ms, verification 50.7±7.5 ms, witness 27.6±5.9 ms, n=30); p. 10 Table V (end-to-end mean 1,582.8±512.9 ms); pp. 11–13 Tables VIII–IX (category breakdown & bypass remediation).
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Parafrasa penulis: NiyamAI mengikat Intent Contract dan aksi agen dengan komitmen SHA-256, mengevaluasi setiap pemanggilan alat melalui gerbang otoritas deterministik dan Judge neural (11->8->2), serta menghasilkan bukti zkSNARK Halo2KZG via EZKL sebelum eksekusi diizinkan.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Diaudit ulang oleh Reviewer 2 dari PDF 2608.07167v2 (15 hlm.): mencakup bukti sketsa Theorem 1, microbenchmark ZK (n=30, Table III), dan evaluasi 2.000 skenario AgentSafetyBench (Tables IV–VIII).
Protected_Object: Committed Intent Contract (IntentHash), tool invocation parameters, and neural Judge evaluation integrity
Composition_Evidence: Menggabungkan pengikatan kontrak niat SHA-256 (B1) dengan intersep pra-eksekusi dan pembuktian Halo2KZG atas evaluasi Judge (B3), tetapi ekstraksi fitur dari argumen alat ke vektor 11 dimensi berada di luar sirkuit ZK.
Coding_Rationale: Audit & Penyempurnaan Reviewer 2 atas draf pilot CLM-0003: Pemeriksaan langsung PDF 2608.07167v2 mengonfirmasi penggunaan EZKL + Halo2KZG (431 rows, logrows=15) dan melengkapi metrik end-to-end Table V (1.582,8 ± 512,9 ms) serta akurasi AgentSafetyBench (88,8% F1, 1,0% FPR; 99,6% blokir aksi berbahaya). Kode limitasi disempurnakan menjadi DG;AD karena selain asumsi TCB ekstraksi fitur dan SRS lokal (AD), evaluasi menunjukkan celah deteksi pada kategori moderasi konten semantik dan ketidakkonsistenan statistik internal p95 < median pada Table III (DG).
Required_Additional_Evidence: Telah diaudit penuh oleh Reviewer 2 terhadap PDF ter-pin; menunggu pengesahan Reviewer 1 pada REVIEW_AUDIT dan resolusi flag konflik statistik Table III (p95 vs median) pada EVALUASI_EMPIRIS_OVERHEAD_RQ3.

Study_Title: NiyamAI - An Intent-Bound AI Agent with Cryptographically Verifiable Guardrails using Zero-Knowledge Proofs

Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NiyamAI learned Judge on AgentSafetyBench with cryptographic proof of its computation.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Judge decision before execution gate.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Semantic unsafe-action classification has residual false negatives even if the Judge computation is faithfully proved.
Trust_Assumptions: AgentSafetyBench labels, cross-validation splits and Judge execution; classifier generalization is separate from SNARK soundness.

Exposed_Security_Function: Classify proposed action safety; a proof authenticates computation, not label correctness.

Evidence_Quote_and_Page: PARAPHRASE; PDF p.9 Table IV and confusion-matrix paragraph; pp.10-13 ablation/discussion.
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Parafrasa sumber: NiyamAI reports 23 unsafe scenarios incorrectly accepted by its Judge in the specified 2000-scenario classification evaluation.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Classifier semantic false negatives in the reported benchmark; not demonstrated compromise of SHA-256 or Halo2KZG.

Study_Title: MCP Security Bench (MSB): Benchmarking Attacks Against Model Context Protocol in LLM Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Adversarial MCP tool providers and poisoned external resources executing 12 single and mixed attack types across tool signatures/descriptions (name collision, preference manipulation, prompt injection), parameters (out-of-scope parameter), tool responses (user impersonation, false error, tool transfer), and retrieval injection.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Non-cryptographic empirical attack benchmark (MCP Security Bench / MSB) and evaluation of prompt-based/detector-based defenses across real MCP tool execution pipelines.
Enforcement_Point_Location: MCP Host Orchestrator, Tool Selection/Invocation Interface, and Tool Response Handler (benchmark evaluation surface)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Empirical vulnerability characterization via Attack Success Rate (ASR), Performance Under Attack (PUA), and Net Resilient Performance (NRP = PUA * (1 - ASR)) across 2,000 attack instances, 10 domains, and 405 MCP tools on 10 LLM backbones (overall average ASR 40.35%, Table 3).
Trust_Assumptions: MCP client host executes tool calls over standard MCP interfaces without cryptographic tool-provider authentication, signed tool schemas, or parameter-scope isolation.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: PDF pp. 7–10 Tables 3, 4, 11–13 (2,000 attack instances across 10 LLM backbones and 405 tools): overall average ASR 40.35%; Out-of-Scope Parameter (OP) highest average ASR 76.50% (min 36.25% on Gemini 2.5 Flash); User Impersonation (UI) average ASR 45.69% (up to 91.80%); False Error (FE) average ASR 39.21% (up to 85.25%); enabling Qwen3-8B thinking mode raises PUA to 64.97% but increases ASR from 47.23% to 57.08%. Runtime latency overhead in ms is NOT_REPORTED.
Exposed_Security_Function: NOT_APPLICABLE — empirical attack benchmark and behavioral robustness metric (NRP), not a cryptographic primitive
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Demonstrates severe empirical security failures across all 10 tested LLM backbones (average ASR 40.35%, peaking at 76.5% for parameter abuse and >85% on mixed/response attacks); evaluated baseline defenses fail to eliminate high-capability instruction-following vulnerability, and no cryptographic authorization or schema-signing countermeasure is implemented.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: PARAFRASA dan kutipan metrik terukur. PDF p. 4 Section 3.2 (threat model); pp. 4–6 Section 4 & Table 1 (12 attack taxonomy); pp. 7–10 Sections 5–6 & Tables 2–4 (2,000 instances, 405 tools, 10 LLMs, average ASR 40.35%, OP ASR 76.5%, UI ASR 45.69%, FE ASR 39.21%); pp. 18–20 Appendix Tables 11–13 (complete single, mixed, and thinking-mode results).
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Parafrasa penulis: MSB mengevaluasi ketahanan 10 agen LLM terhadap 12 jenis serangan spesifik-MCP (2.000 instans pada 405 alat nyata) di sepanjang perencanaan tugas, pemanggilan alat, dan penanganan respons menggunakan metrik ASR, PUA, dan Net Resilient Performance (NRP).
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Benchmark eksperimental end-to-end pada 10 model LLM dan 405 alat MCP di 10 domain; mengukur tingkat keberhasilan serangan (ASR) dan utilitas (PUA/NRP), tanpa pengujian overhead latensi kriptografi.
Protected_Object: MCP tool selection, tool invocation parameters, tool response handling, and agent planning context
Composition_Evidence: Mengevaluasi serangan tunggal dan campuran (mixed attacks di Table 12) yang melintasi batas pemilihan alat/parameter (B2) dan respons eksekusi alat (B3), membuktikan bahwa serangan komposit menghasilkan ASR yang lebih tinggi daripada serangan tunggal.
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi & Verifikasi Reviewer 2: Studi Stream A murni yang memberikan bukti empiris kuat mengenai kegagalan batas B2;B3 pada protokol MCP tanpa jaminan kriptografi (kode limitasi DG karena rata-rata ASR 40,35% dan OP mencapai 76,5%). Formal_Evidence_Type adalah NONE dan PQC_Migration_Stage adalah NOT_DISCUSSED sesuai isi sumber.
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi silang Reviewer 1 pada REVIEW_AUDIT dan pencatatan metrik ASR/PUA/NRP (Tables 3, 11, 12, 13) pada sheet EVALUASI_EMPIRIS_OVERHEAD_RQ3.

Study_Title: HDP: A Lightweight Cryptographic Protocol for Human Delegation Provenance in Agentic AI Systems
Threat_Attacker_Model: Unauthorised or prompt-injected sub-agent in a multi-hop delegation chain attempting to forge human principal authorization, tamper with or reorder prior delegation hops, or replay expired/cross-session delegation tokens.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Human Delegation Provenance (HDP v0.1) token protocol using Ed25519 digital signatures (RFC 8032, noble-ed25519) over RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS) with append-only chained hop signatures and session/expiry binding.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Orchestrator, Intermediate Sub-Agents, and Terminal Tool-Execution Agent Verifier (7-step offline verification pipeline)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Token unforgeability and append-only delegation chain tamper detection reduced to Ed25519 EUF-CMA security over Curve25519/SHA-512 (Sections 5.1–5.2, p. 8), plus bounded replay defense via session_id and expires_at (24h default).
Trust_Assumptions: Confidentiality of the issuer's Ed25519 private key (stored in HSM/secrets manager); honest human principal issuance; application-layer enforcement of semantic alignment between scope.intent and actual tool action.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: PDF p. 7 & pp. 9–10 Section 6.3: analytical/order-of-magnitude claims only ('Ed25519 signature verification completing in under 100 microseconds', 'a 10-hop token with typical field values is approximately 4–8 KB'); no controlled experimental benchmark table or sample size n is reported in the manuscript.
Exposed_Security_Function: Ed25519 token issuance, chained hop signature extension, and 7-step offline chain verification
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Section 7.1 (p. 10) explicitly notes that HDP v0.1 uses a single shared issuer Ed25519 key for all hop signatures rather than per-agent keypairs (so hop signatures attest recording by the issuer, not independent agent identity until v0.2); Section 5.4 & 7.2 (pp. 9–10) state that HDP does not enforce semantic consistency between action_summary and scope.intent; performance numbers (<100 us, 4–8 KB) are analytical estimates without experimental tables.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: PARAFRASA dan kutipan spesifikasi protokol. PDF pp. 4–5 Section 3 (threat model); pp. 6–8 Section 4 & Figure 1 (token structure, RFC 8785 JCS, Ed25519, 7-step verification); pp. 8–9 Sections 5.1–5.6 (EUF-CMA reduction & semantic boundary); pp. 9–10 Sections 6–7 (@helixar_ai/hdp TypeScript SDK, <100 us & 4–8 KB analytical estimates, v0.1 single-key limitation).
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Parafrasa penulis: HDP mengikat peristiwa otorisasi manusia ke sesi dan mencatat setiap delegasi agen sebagai hop bertanda tangan Ed25519 di atas JSON kanonis RFC 8785 dalam rantai append-only yang dapat diverifikasi secara offline menggunakan kunci publik Ed25519 penerbit.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Spesifikasi protokol HDP v0.1 (IETF Internet-Draft draft-helixar-hdp-agentic-delegation-00), argumen reduksi EUF-CMA Ed25519, dan implementasi referensi SDK TypeScript tanpa tabel benchmark eksperimental.
Protected_Object: Human authorization root context, delegation scope, and multi-hop agent provenance chain
Composition_Evidence: Menghubungkan otorisasi prinsipal manusia (B1) dengan delegasi antar-agen (B2) dan jejak audit pasca-eksekusi (B4), tetapi penulis menyatakan penegakan semantik runtime memerlukan integrasi eksternal (mis. MI9 atau CaMeL, Section 7.2 p. 10).
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi & Verifikasi Reviewer 2: Studi memenuhi Stream M pada B1;B2;B4. Kode AD diberikan karena ketergantungan penuh pada satu kunci privat Ed25519 milik issuer untuk seluruh hop pada v0.1 (Section 7.1, p. 10) serta ketiadaan penegakan semantik atas action_summary terhadap prompt injection yang memanipulasi agen sah (Section 5.4, p. 9).
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi silang Reviewer 1 pada REVIEW_AUDIT; catat bahwa angka latensi (<100 us) dan ukuran token (4–8 KB) pada Section 6.3 bersifat estimasi analitis tanpa tabel eksperimen.

Study_Title: Securing LLM-Agent Long-Term Memory Against Poisoning: Non-Malleable, Origin-Bound Authority with Machine-Checked Guarantees
Threat_Attacker_Model: Cross-session memory poisoning adversary planting untrusted content that is laundered across sessions via three agent-specific channels: (1) agent self-summarization, (2) trusted-tool echo, and (3) Sybil/manufactured corroboration to trigger unauthorized consequential actions.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: TMA-NM (Tamper-evident Memory Authority, Non-Malleable): write-time origin-bound authority labels, monotone meet derivation propagation, Sybil-resistant corroboration-gated elevation (>=k independent trusted principals), TLA+/TLC machine-checked model, and local SHA-256 hash-chained verdict log.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Memory Write/Retrieve Monitor and Pre-Execution Consequential Action Gate (act-gate)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Machine-checked TLA+/TLC Theorems 1–3 (across 3,270 reachable states and unbounded inductive invariant IndInv, p. 4) and empirical 0.0% consequential-action ASR across direct and all 3 laundering channels over 8 frontier models at 95.9–100% legitimate utility (Tables I–V, pp. 5–7).
Trust_Assumptions: Assumption A1 (p. 2): write-time principal channel authentication (e.g., mTLS, audience-bound OAuth, or signed tool responses) is provided by the underlying substrate; monitor and act-gate cannot be bypassed by the LLM.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: PDF pp. 5–7 Tables I–V (8 frontier models across 6 vendors; 4 reproduced published attacks in Table V n=1,152 attack runs + 384 benign runs): TMA-NM achieves 0.0% consequential-action ASR (0/192 per laundering channel, 0/1,152 on drop-in attacks vs 38.2% undefended, 19.6% lineage, 12.0% prob_detect) with 95.9%–100% legitimate utility and microsecond-scale in-memory gate decision latency ('adds no perceptible latency', p. 5).
Exposed_Security_Function: Write-time origin authority tagging, corroboration-threshold gate verification, and SHA-256 hash-chained verdict logging

Study_Title: Heartbeat-Bound Hierarchical Credentials: Cryptographic Revocation for AI Agent Swarms
Threat_Attacker_Model: Rogue or compromised sub-agent ('zombie agent') continuing to execute tool/API actions after parent orchestrator crash, revocation, or network partition severing control-plane connectivity to the Identity Provider (IdP).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Heartbeat-Bound Hierarchical Credentials (HBHC): ECDSA secp256k1 (or P-256) signatures, HMAC-SHA256 key derivation, BIP-32 hardened hierarchical key derivation, and SHA-256 epoch/policy commitments enforced via sliding freshness window W_max = k * Delta_h.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Stateless Local Tool/Resource Verifier Gate (verifying parent heartbeat + child capability proof offline)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Theorem 1 (Bounded Zombie Window <= k * Delta_h + delta_clock) and Theorem 2 (Partition-Tolerant Revocation) reduced to ECDSA EUF-CMA under CDH and SHA-256 collision resistance (Section 4, p. 6), achieving 90x zombie-window reduction (39.2 s vs 3,600 s OAuth TTL) and 100% denial at epoch 4 (Tables 3–4).
Trust_Assumptions: Parent heartbeat signing keys protected in HSM/TPM/TEE; synchronized clocks within bounded skew delta_clock; standard ECDSA CDH and SHA-256 hardness (quantum adversaries explicitly excluded in Section 3, p. 4).
Performance_Overhead_Reported: PDF pp. 7–10 Tables 3–7 & Appendices A–D (Apple M2 workstation, Python 1,200 LOC & Rust k256/actix-web): Rust full verification latency 0.21–0.26 ms per request (O(1) from N=10 to 10,000 agents, ~4,800 verifications/s single-core); heartbeat payload 168 bytes; end-to-end overhead across 5 coding/review tasks 0.71% (19,700 ms with HBHC vs 19,560 ms baseline); measured zombie window 8.1 s (Delta_h=2s) and 39.2 s (Delta_h=10s) vs 3,600 s OAuth TTL (90x reduction).
Exposed_Security_Function: BIP-32/HMAC-SHA256 hierarchical credential derivation, periodic ECDSA heartbeat signing, and stateless offline freshness verification
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Actions remain permitted during the residual zombie window W_max (up to 39.2 s at Delta_h=10s) before heartbeat expiry; requires bounded clock skew delta_clock between parent and verifier (Table 7 shows window inflation under clock lag); packet loss >=10% without pre-emptive 2x heartbeat sending causes false-positive revocation (Table 6).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: PARAFRASA dan kutipan metrik terukur. PDF p. 4 Section 3 & Table 2 (threat model & PQC note: SPHINCS+/Dilithium substitution); pp. 5–6 Section 4 & Theorems 1–2 (ECDSA secp256k1, HMAC-SHA256, BIP-32); pp. 7–10 Section 6 & Tables 3–7 (zombie window 39.2 s vs 3,600 s, Rust verify 0.21–0.26 ms, 168-byte heartbeat, 0.71% E2E overhead).
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Parafrasa penulis: HBHC mengikat kredensial kapabilitas sub-agen ke detak jantung (heartbeat) kriptografis periodik bertanda tangan ECDSA dari agen induk sehingga pencabutan wewenang berlaku secara pasif dan offline dalam jendela deterministik W_max meskipun terjadi partisi jaringan.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Bukti reduksi keamanan (Theorems 1–2) dan evaluasi benchmark implementasi Python/Rust dari 10 hingga 10.000 agen konkuren, injeksi kehilangan paket/latensi WAN (Linux tc), dan 5 tugas agen end-to-end.
Protected_Object: Hierarchical sub-agent capability credentials and temporal execution liveness authority
Composition_Evidence: Mengikat delegasi hierarkis induk-ke-anak (B1;B2) secara langsung dengan verifikasi gerbang eksekusi alat offline (B3) melalui gabungan bukti kapabilitas anak dan heartbeat induk terbaru.
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi & Verifikasi Reviewer 2: Studi memenuhi Stream M_AND_A pada B1;B2;B3 dengan bukti reduksi formal (Theorems 1–2) dan eksperimen partisi/overhead yang sangat lengkap (Tables 3–7). Kode AD diberikan karena ketergantungan pada sinkronisasi jam (delta_clock), perlindungan kunci induk di HSM/TEE, dan jendela aktif residual selama W_max. Halaman 4 secara eksplisit menyebutkan substitusi ECDSA dengan tanda tangan pasca-kuantum SPHINCS+ atau Dilithium (STAGE_1_SUGGESTED_MIGRATION).

Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Agent Name Service (ANS): W3C DIDs and Verifiable Credentials, hierarchical X.509 PKI with automated Sigstore certificate provisioning, Istio service-mesh mutual TLS (mTLS), and Open Policy Agent (OPA) admission/runtime policy gates.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Kubernetes Admission Controller, ANS Registry Resolver, OPA Policy Engine, and Istio Service Mesh Sidecar Proxy

Study_Title: Proof-of-Guardrail in AI Agents and What (Not) to Trust from It
Threat_Attacker_Model: Dishonest or negligent online agent developer falsely advertising that agent responses pass through a specific open-source safety/factuality guardrail, or tampering with guardrail code, attestation bytes, or responses.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Proof-of-Guardrail: AWS Nitro Enclaves hardware TEE remote attestation signing PCR2 measurement of the open-source guardrail wrapper f and SHA-256 digest of the (input x, response r) pair, verifiable offline against the AWS Nitro root certificate.
Enforcement_Point_Location: AWS Nitro Enclave TEE Wrapper (hosting OpenClaw agent + Llama Guard 3-8B / Loki guardrail) and Client Offline Verifier
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Cryptographically verifiable integrity that a specific measured open-source guardrail code (PCR2) executed on exact input x and approved output r inside an AWS Nitro Enclave (100% detection across 10/10 code modifications, 100/100 attestation-byte modifications, and 100/100 response modifications in Table 1, p. 4).
Trust_Assumptions: Uncompromised AWS Nitro Enclave hardware/firmware root of trust and attestation key; open-source guardrail wrapper f is free of developer backdoors and audited by the community.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: PDF p. 4 Section 4.3 & Table 2 (OpenClaw on AWS m5.xlarge Nitro Enclave): attestation generation 97.8 ± 4.2 ms; offline attestation verification 5.1 ± 0.0 ms; ToxicChat response + Llama Guard 3-8B latency 2,828 ± 1,663 ms in TEE vs 2,050 ± 531 ms non-TEE (+38.0% overhead; 25%–38% range, 34% avg); EC2 hourly cost $0.192/hr vs $0.0104/hr (18.5x).
Exposed_Security_Function: AWS Nitro Enclave PCR2 code measurement, SHA-256 I/O binding, and hardware-signed attestation verification
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Authors explicitly demonstrate and emphasize (Abstract, Section 3.3, Section 5, Table 3) that Proof-of-Guardrail proves guardrail execution, NOT agent safety: a malicious developer whose private agent A is unmeasured or adversarial can actively jailbreak or exploit false negatives in the guardrail, or selectively omit/cherry-pick executions.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: PARAFRASA dan kutipan metrik terukur. PDF p. 3 Section 3 & Figure 2 (TEE enclave architecture & PCR2 attestation binding); p. 4 Sections 4.1–4.3 & Tables 1–3 (10/10 code tamper, 100/100 sig tamper, 100/100 response tamper detected; 25%–38% / 34% avg TEE latency overhead, +100 ms attestation generation, 18.5x EC2 cost overhead); p. 5 Sections 5–6 (residual deception/jailbreak risks).

Study_Title: Right to History: A Sovereignty Kernel for Verifiable AI Agent Execution
Threat_Attacker_Model: Level 1 adversary (compromised or misbehaving AI agent / untrusted skill plugin on personal hardware) attempting out-of-scope file/system writes, resource exhaustion, history fabrication/omission, or bypassing human approval; Level 2 root/OS attacker modifying disk storage post-hoc is detectable only if Merkle checkpoints were exported externally.

Study_Title: Tool Receipts, Not Zero-Knowledge Proofs: Practical Hallucination Detection for AI Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Hallucinating or compromised LLM agent fabricating tool executions, misstating output counts, claiming false absence, or fabricating URLs in its final response without actually invoking the underlying tool or matching its output.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: NabaOS epistemic verification framework: runtime-generated HMAC-SHA256 tool execution receipts (binding tool name, SHA-256 input/output digests, timestamp, and extracted facts with a secret key inaccessible to the LLM) paired with pramana claim classification and cross-referencing.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Sandboxed Tool Execution Runtime Wrapper (HMAC receipt issuer) and Post-Generation Response Verifier
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Unforgeability of tool execution receipts against the LLM under HMAC-SHA256 key secrecy, detecting 91.0% of injected hallucinations overall (94.2% fabricated tool calls, 87.6% count misstatements, 91.3% false absence claims) at 4.0% FPR across 1,800 NyayaVerifyBench scenarios (Tables 3–4, pp. 9–10).
Trust_Assumptions: Agent host runtime and sandbox wrapper holding the HMAC-SHA256 secret key are trusted and uncompromised; external tools return truthful data (malicious tool operators or compromised host runtimes are explicitly out of scope, Section 6 p. 11).
Performance_Overhead_Reported: PDF pp. 9–11 Section 5 & Tables 3–7 (NyayaVerifyBench, 1,800 scenarios across 4 languages): NabaOS local HMAC receipt + pramana verification adds +12 ms mean overhead per response (<15 ms, $0 cost/req, 91% detection, 4% FPR) vs +2 ms Output Regex (35% detection) and +3,000–5,000 ms LLM-as-Judge; deep-agent web cross-checking (URL re-fetching) adds 200–500 ms latency and catches 78.4% of URL fabrications.
Exposed_Security_Function: HMAC-SHA256 tool receipt generation/verification and epistemic claim-to-receipt cross-checking
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Misses 9.0% of injected hallucinations overall (and 21.6% of deep-agent URL fabrications) with a 4.0% false positive rate (Table 3); HMAC key resides in the local agent runtime, so it provides zero protection against a compromised host/operator (unlike receiver-attested Sello in ARXIV-S-0029) and cannot detect lying external tools (Section 6, p. 11).

PDF pp. 5–6 Sections 3.2–3.3 (HMAC-SHA256 receipt schema & verifier); pp. 8–10 Sections 4–5 & Tables 2–6 (NyayaVerifyBench 1,800 scenarios, 91% aggregate detection, 94.2% fabricated tool detection, 4% FPR, +12 ms / <15 ms verification overhead, 200–500 ms deep cross-checking); p. 11 Section 6 & Table 7 (ZK comparison & runtime trust / malicious tool limitations).

Study_Title: "MCP Does Not Stand for Misuse Cryptography Protocol": Uncovering Cryptographic Misuse in Model Context Protocol at Scale

Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: MICRYSCOPE: cross-language static AST/IR normalizer, hybrid explicit/implicit LLM-orchestrated dependency analyzer, and interprocedural taint-analysis detector evaluating 8 cryptographic misuse rules (R1–R8) across 9,403 MCP servers.

Security_Property_Guaranteed: Large-scale empirical vulnerability measurement across 9,403 real-world MCP servers from 7 registries: identifies 720 servers containing cryptographic logic, of which 142 (19.72%) exhibit concrete cryptographic API misuses across rules R1–R8 (95% precision in manual validation of 100 sampled servers, Section 5.2–5.3, pp. 13–16).
Trust_Assumptions: Static AST/IR rules and taint source/sink definitions accurately model target language crypto APIs (obfuscated string concatenation or custom wrapper functions can cause false negatives, Figure 10 p. 14).

Exposed_Security_Function: NOT_APPLICABLE — static taint/AST vulnerability analyzer auditing cryptographic API misuse in MCP servers
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Uncovers widespread cryptographic implementation defects in deployed MCP servers (19.7% misuse rate among crypto-using servers, led by R7 Missing Integrity Protection / unauthenticated encryption at 81 servers, R5 Hardcoded Keys at 24, and R3 Weak Hash MD5/SHA-1); MICRYSCOPE itself is an offline static scanner that can miss obfuscated wrappers (5% false negative/inaccuracy rate, Fig. 10 p. 14).

Study_Title: Notarized Agents: Receiver-Attested Confidential Receipts for AI Agent Actions
Threat_Attacker_Model: Compromised or dishonest agent and untrusted hosting operator attempting to fabricate, alter, or selectively omit activity logs, plus curious transparency-log observers attempting to infer sensitive action payloads from public logs.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Sello v0.1 receiver-attested confidential receipt protocol: COSE_Sign1 (Ed25519) signing by the called service, single-shot HPKE payload encryption (X25519 KEM, HKDF-SHA256, ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD) to owner public key bound in JWS authorization token, SHA-256 input/output digests, and witness-cosigned Merkle transparency log (Sigstore Rekor style).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Receiving External Tool/Service Endpoint (receipt signer/encryptor) and Agent Owner Offline Audit Reconstructor
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Unforgeable receiver-attested action receipts (P1), payload confidentiality against public log observers (P2), append-only non-repudiation with log-integrated-time revocation resistance against backdating (P3), and owner-side discovery via sello_token_ref = SHA-256(token) (P4) (Sections 4–5, pp. 8–13).
Trust_Assumptions: Called external service is honest and does not collude with a malicious operator to fabricate receipts; owner HPKE private key and JWS token issuer key are secure; witness-cosigned transparency log maintains split-view resistance.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: PDF pp. 15–16 Section 7.2 & Tables 1–2 (TypeScript/Node.js v0.1 microbenchmark, N=1,000 steady-state over 10 runs): full COSE_Sign1 + HPKE receipt wire size is fixed at 467 bytes (234B CBOR body, 112B header, 282B HPKE ciphertext; mock log proof 253B); service receipt creation median 0.454 ms (p95 0.954 ms, p99 1.534 ms); owner single-receipt verification + HPKE decryption median 0.281 ms (p95 0.573 ms, p99 1.034 ms); batch verification 0.320 ms/receipt (first-party public log network RTT not measured).
Exposed_Security_Function: Ed25519 COSE_Sign1 receipt signing, X25519/ChaCha20-Poly1305 HPKE sealing/opening, JWS owner-key binding, and Merkle inclusion verification
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Sections 5.5 & 8.1 (pp. 12–13, 17–19) explicitly identify four open limitations: (1) suppression attack (if an agent simply does not call a service, no receipt is emitted), (2) service-operator collusion, (3) sello_token_ref linkability/enumeration across receipts from the same token on the public log, and (4) v0.1 reliance on a static JSON-file service identity registry and zero current third-party service adoption incentive.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: PARAFRASA dan kutipan metrik terukur. PDF p. 4 Section 2.1 (COSE_Sign1 Ed25519, HPKE X25519/HKDF-SHA256/ChaCha20-Poly1305, JWS); pp. 8–10 Section 4 (CDDL receipt structure, 8-step owner verification, log-integrated time revocation); pp. 15–16 Section 7.2 & Tables 1–2 (467-byte envelope, N=1000 create median 0.454 ms, verify median 0.281 ms); pp. 17–19 Section 8 (suppression attack, static JSON registry, token_ref linkability).
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Parafrasa penulis: Sello membalik batas kepercayaan observabilitas agen dengan meminta layanan penerima menandatangani tanda terima aksi (COSE_Sign1 Ed25519), mengenkripsinya dengan HPKE ke kunci publik pemilik yang terikat pada token JWS, dan mempublikasikannya ke log transparansi Merkle.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Spesifikasi protokol Sello v0.1, analisis keamanan terhadap operator agen yang tidak dipercaya, dan microbenchmark operasi kriptografi lokal (N=10, 100, 1.000) tanpa pengukuran latensi jaringan log publik.
Protected_Object: Confidential receiver-attested action receipts (input/output SHA-256 hashes, status, timestamp) and owner audit trail
Composition_Evidence: Mengikat kunci publik HPKE pemilik di dalam token otorisasi JWS ke tanda terima COSE_Sign1/HPKE yang diterbitkan layanan penerima pada log Merkle (B4).

Study_Title: Fairly Compensated Distributed Information Retrieval and Augmentation for AI Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Curious distributed data providers attempting to infer a querying agent's confidential prompt/interest during federated RAG discovery, and mutually distrusting searching/providing agents attempting to cheat during atomic information-value exchange (free-riding without paying or taking payment without revealing the valid decryption key).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Two-phase decentralized agentic RAG protocol: (Phase 1) BGV Threshold Homomorphic Encryption (THE, OpenFHE) for encrypted cosine-similarity relevance scoring across distributed providers; (Phase 2) Atomic Information-Value Exchange combining Groth16 zk-SNARKs (Circom), Poseidon hash commitments, and Ethereum Hashed Timelock Smart Contracts (HTLC).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Distributed Agentic RAG Relevance Evaluation Protocol and Ethereum Smart Contract HTLC Verifier
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Query/document confidentiality during relevance scoring under BGV RLWE hardness, and fair atomic exchange of encrypted knowledge for payment under Groth16 knowledge-soundness and Poseidon collision resistance on Ethereum HTLC (Section 3, pp. 5–9).
Trust_Assumptions: Honest majority / non-collusion threshold among THE decryption shareholders; Groth16 trusted setup (Powers of Tau) and Poseidon collision resistance; timely transaction inclusion on Ethereum before HTLC timelock expiry.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: PDF pp. 13–15 Section 5 & Tables 1–5 (OpenFHE BGV, Circom Groth16, Hardhat & Sepolia, n=20): Phase 1 homomorphic Poseidon hash evaluation scales from 6.59 s (2B input) to 86.72 s (32B input) while scorer takes 0.02–0.04 s (Table 1); Poseidon HTLC withdraw uses 75,263 gas vs 86,896 gas for SHA-256 (-13.4%, Table 3); local Hardhat latency 79.50–91.25 ms (Table 4); Sepolia latency dominated by block confirmation (Table 5).
Exposed_Security_Function: BGV threshold homomorphic inner-product evaluation, Poseidon hashing, Groth16 zk-SNARK proof verification, and HTLC settlement
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Groth16 Powers-of-Tau setup and circuit size scale with document block size (Table 2, p. 13); Sepolia settlement latency (~12–15 s) and gas price volatility limit real-time sub-second agent loops; relies on threshold non-collusion in Phase 1 and timely blockchain liveness before timelock refund in Phase 2.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: PARAFRASA dan kutipan metrik terukur. PDF pp. 5–9 Section 3 (Phase 1 BGV THE relevance discovery & Phase 2 Groth16 + Poseidon HTLC atomic exchange); pp. 13–15 Section 4 & Tables 1–5 (Table 1 Phase 1 timings, Table 2 Powers of Tau scaling, Table 3 Poseidon vs SHA-256 gas: withdraw 75,263 vs 86,896 gas [-13.4%], Table 4 Hardhat latency 79.50–91.25 ms, Table 5 Sepolia latency n=20).
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Parafrasa penulis: Protokol dua fase ini memungkinkan agen pencari mengevaluasi relevansi informasi secara privat menggunakan Threshold Homomorphic Encryption (BGV) dan mengeksekusi pertukaran nilai-informasi atomik tanpa pihak ketiga tepercaya menggunakan zk-SNARK Groth16, hash Poseidon, dan kontrak pintar HTLC Ethereum.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Evaluasi eksperimental purwarupa menggunakan OpenFHE (BGV), Circom (Groth16), serta jaringan lokal Hardhat dan testnet Ethereum Sepolia (20 run, Tables 1–5).
Protected_Object: Confidential agent search queries, distributed provider knowledge chunks, and atomic payment-for-key settlement
Composition_Evidence: Mengomposisikan pemilihan penyedia pengetahuan berbasis relevansi terenkripsi THE (B2) dengan eksekusi pertukaran kunci-dan-pembayaran atomik menggunakan Groth16 + HTLC (B3).
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi & Verifikasi Reviewer 2: Sesuai adjudikasi Stage 2 (Stream M), studi ini mengoperasionalkan seleksi dan transaksi agen terdesentralisasi dengan metrik gas dan latensi lengkap (Tables 1–5). Kode AD diberikan karena ketergantungan pada non-kolusi pemegang saham kunci THE, trusted setup Groth16, dan asumsi liveness blok Ethereum sebelum batas waktu HTLC berakhir.

Study_Title: Agent Audit: A Security Analysis System for LLM Agent Applications
Threat_Attacker_Model: Vulnerabilities in LLM agent application stacks across all 10 OWASP Agentic Security Initiative (ASI) categories: untrusted LLM output flowing to dangerous sinks (SQLi, eval/RCE, SSRF), exposed credentials, over-privileged MCP configurations, cross-server tool shadowing, and tool description poisoning.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Non-cryptographic static & configuration security analyzer (Agent Audit): 57 detection rules combining Python AST taint/dataflow analysis, credential scanning, MCP JSON/YAML schema/privilege parsing, Levenshtein tool-shadowing checks, and 4-tier confidence scoring.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Pre-Deployment Local CLI / GitHub Actions CI/CD Gate and Live MCP `inspect` Stdio Scanner
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Detects 40 of 42 annotated vulnerabilities (95.24% recall, 86.96% precision, 6 false positives) across 22 agent projects on Agent-Vuln-Bench (AVB), achieving 100% recall on injection/RCE (Set A) and MCP configuration/supply-chain (Set B) vulnerabilities where Semgrep and Bandit achieve 0% on MCP configs (Table 2 & Figure 3, pp. 3–4).
Trust_Assumptions: Agent source code and MCP configuration manifests are available to the CI/CD scanner prior to execution; heuristic confidence thresholds (BLOCK >=0.92, WARN >=0.60) are empirically calibrated.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: PDF pp. 1, 3–4 Abstract, Section 3.2, Table 2 & Figure 3 (Agent-Vuln-Bench: 22 samples, 42 vulnerabilities): Agent Audit achieves 95.24% recall (40/42 detected, 6 FPs, 100% on Set A & Set B, 85.7% on Set C) with 'sub-second scan times' (synthetic Layer 1 fixtures: 98.51% precision at 100% recall).
Exposed_Security_Function: NOT_APPLICABLE — static AST dataflow, MCP configuration, and live stdio description inspection tool

Study_Title: The Stochastic Deputy: Structural Tenant Isolation for Tool-Using LLM Agents
Threat_Attacker_Model: Stochastic/confused deputy attack in multi-tenant MCP tool servers where prompt injection or plausible pretext steers an LLM agent into supplying another tenant's identifier or forging writable scope files/environment variables to read cross-tenant data.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Structural Tenant Isolation: removal of tenant parameters from MCP tool schemas (I1), OAuth 2.1 RS256 JWT access tokens verified via JWKS with RFC 9449 DPoP sender-constrained proofs at the MCP gateway (I2), and database-layer lateral-join (`JSON_TABLE`) scoped predicate enforcement (I3–I5).
Enforcement_Point_Location: MCP Server Auth Gateway (RS256/JWKS + DPoP verifier) and MySQL Database Query Builder / View Layer
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Eliminates parameter-steered cross-tenant reads across 373 adversarial ablation trials on 8 LLM configurations and 2 transports: parameter-exposed baseline leaked 26/26 plausible-pretext trials, schema removal blocked 100% of read-parameter attacks, and RS256/JWKS cryptographic context binding blocked all 12/56 writable-scope forgery escapes and all 7 claim-tampering transformations (Tables 12–15, pp. 13–15).
Trust_Assumptions: Uncompromised OAuth 2.1 authorization server / JWKS key custody; MCP server process and database connection pool sit inside the trusted enforcement boundary below the LLM.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: PDF pp. 10–11 Tables 3–7 & Fig. 4 (production multi-GB MySQL dataset): median query latency JSON_CONTAINS 5,781.24 ms (57x cliff), JSON_TABLE 101.36 ms, deployed builder 453.31 ms (vs 65 ms bare baseline: +387 ms total overhead, of which 346 ms [91%] is soft-delete filter missing index and 36 ms [9%] is ghost-data guard); entitlement-size planner cliff at |S|=15 tenants reaches 638 ms (21.3x single-tenant query).
Exposed_Security_Function: OAuth 2.1 RS256 JWT + JWKS signature verification, DPoP proof validation, and capability-scoped SQL query rewriting
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Without cryptographic token binding, 12 of 56 trials escaped schema removal by overwriting writable local scope files/configs in the CLI harness (Table 14, p. 14); at the database layer, MySQL's query planner switches from index range scan to full table scan when a principal's entitlement set reaches |S|>=15 tenants, causing a 21.3x latency jump (638 ms, Tables 6–7 p. 11).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: PARAFRASA dan kutipan metrik terukur. PDF pp. 5–8 Section 4 & Table 1 (Invariants I1–I5, RS256/JWKS, DPoP); pp. 9–12 Section 6, Tables 3–7 & Figure 4 (57x naive cliff, JSON_TABLE 452 ms vs 65 ms baseline, 36 ms ghost-guard overhead, |S|=15 planner cliff at 638 ms); pp. 13–15 Section 8 & Tables 12–15 (373-trial ablation across 8 LLM configs: 26/26 baseline leak, 12/56 writable-scope escape without crypto binding, 0 leaks with RS256+schema binding).
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Parafrasa penulis: Menghapus parameter identitas tenant dari skema alat MCP, mengikat cakupan tenant ke kredensial JWT RS256/JWKS terverifikasi, dan menegakkannya di lapisan kueri database menggunakan lateral join JSON_TABLE menghentikan serangan confused/stochastic deputy lintas 373 uji coba pada 8 konfigurasi LLM.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Evaluasi ablasi 373 percobaan serangan pada 8 konfigurasi model LLM dan 2 transport (stdio vs HTTP/Bearer),7 uji manipulasi klaim JWT, serta benchmark latensi kueri pada database produksi multi-GB.
Protected_Object: Multi-tenant database records, MCP tool invocation scope, and OAuth 2.1 RS256 tenant-entitlement claims
Composition_Evidence: Membuktikan secara empiris bahwa penghapusan parameter pada skema alat saja (B2) gagal jika agen dapat menulis ke konfigurasi scope lokal (12/56 lolos), sehingga wajib dikomposisikan dengan pengikatan token kriptografis RS256/JWKS dan penegakan predikat SQL di bawah agen (B3).
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi & Verifikasi Reviewer 2: Studi memenuhi Stream M_AND_A pada B2;B3 dengan bukti empiris yang sangat kaya baik untuk serangan (373 trial) maupun dekomposisi overhead database (Tables 3–15). Study_Title: Security awareness in LLM agents: the NDAI zone case
Threat_Attacker_Model: Unverified or spoofed execution environment claims ('you are running inside a TEE') and failing/passing remote attestation tool outputs (`verify_tee_attestation`) influencing an inventor LLM agent's decision to disclose confidential intellectual property during NDAI bilateral negotiation.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Simulated TEE remote attestation tool (`verify_tee_attestation` returning true/false in an Intel TDX NDAI negotiation prompt harness; Section 2.1 p. 4 explicitly notes no real TEE hardware or cryptographic attestation is executed).
Enforcement_Point_Location: LLM Agent Context Window & Tool-Output Interpretation Layer (behavioral evaluation across 10 LLMs)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Empirical behavioral finding across 2,000 negotiation runs (10 frontier LLMs x 4 attestation scenarios): a failing attestation (`false`) universally suppresses IP disclosure below the no-TEE baseline across all 10 models, whereas a passing attestation (`true`) yields highly heterogeneous, uncalibrated responses (some models increase disclosure, others are unaffected, and several paradoxically reduce disclosure, Figure 2–6 & Table 2 p. 10).
Trust_Assumptions: Evaluates whether LLM agents can form calibrated security awareness from context-window text claims and attestation tool outputs assuming the NDAI TEE protocol itself would delete data on failed deals.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: PDF pp. 5–8 Section 3 & p. 10 Appendix Table 2 (2,000 negotiation runs across 10 LLMs and 4 scenarios): reports mean IP disclosure scores (0 to 1 scale) and Credulity/Verification Effect (CE_m, VE_m) per model; runtime latency overhead in ms is NOT_REPORTED because experiments were executed outside a real TEE to save cost and time (Section 2.1 p. 4).
Exposed_Security_Function: Simulated `verify_tee_attestation` tool call returning mocked boolean attestation status in prompt context
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Demonstrates a fundamental security-awareness gap in frontier LLMs: models treat unverified prompt claims of TEE security credulously or react paradoxically to passing `verify_tee_attestation` tool outputs, proving that exposing cryptographic attestation results directly to an LLM's context window does not yield reliable security calibration (DG); all TEE attestations in the study are simulated mocks rather than real hardware enclaves (AD).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: PARAFRASA dan kutipan metrik terukur. PDF p. 4 Section 2.1 (4 scenarios: No-TEE, TEE text claim, attestation=true, attestation=false; explicit note that agents do not run in a real TEE); pp. 5–8 Section 3 & Figures 2–6 (asymmetry between danger detection and safety verification across 10 LLMs); p. 10 Appendix Table 2 (mean disclosure scores over 2,000 runs).
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Parafrasa penulis: Evaluasi atas 10 model LLM dalam tugas negosiasi NDAI menunjukkan asimetri tajam: hasil atestasi TEE yang gagal secara universal menekan pengungkapan rahasia, tetapi atestasi yang berhasil menghasilkan respons yang tidak terkalibrasi dan heterogen, membuktikan bahwa agen LLM tidak dapat memverifikasi keamanan lingkungan eksekusinya secara andal hanya dari bukti di jendela konteks.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Simulasi perilaku 2.000 run negosiasi lintas 10 model LLM pada 4 skenario bukti atestasi TEE yang di-mock di luar perangkat keras TEE nyata.
Protected_Object: Confidential inventor intellectual property (IP) disclosure decisions during multi-agent negotiation

Study_Title: Governing Dynamic Capabilities: Cryptographic Binding and Reproducibility Verification for AI Agent Tool Use
Threat_Attacker_Model: Silent capability escalation (acquiring undeclared tools at runtime), tool trojanization, adversarial model substitution/backdooring (QLoRA weight poisoning), phantom delegation exceeding depth/tier bounds, and post-hoc interaction ledger tampering or blame shifting across multi-agent pipelines.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: A2Auth governance stack (`agent-trust-kit` in Rust/PyO3): (G1) Capability-Bound X.509 v3 Agent Certificates with SHA-256 skill-manifest commitments (basic Ed25519 or enhanced BBS+ selective disclosure); (G2) Probabilistic Replay Verification & Groth16 DV-SNARK; (G3) Verifiable Interaction Ledger with bilateral Ed25519 signatures and SHA-256 hash chaining.
Enforcement_Point_Location: MCP Governance Proxy & Multi-Agent Orchestration Trust Layer (Rust `agent-trust-kit` FFI)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Proves Theorem 1 (Bounded Divergence) and Theorem 2 (Chain Verifiability, Section 5 pp. 10–11), detects 99.1%–100% of QLoRA model-backdoor substitutions at budget n>=10 (Table 8 p. 13), prevents/detects all 12 governance attack scenarios (Table 10 p. 15), and detects 7/7 live end-to-end multi-agent attacks vs 0/7 for OAuth 2.1 and OpenTelemetry baselines (Table 14 p. 15).
Trust_Assumptions: Root CA and human tier-0 issuer keys are secure; Ed25519 EUF-CMA, BBS+/Groth16 soundness, and SHA-256 collision resistance hold; temperature=0 inference reproducibility holds within bounded divergence for software G2 replay.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: PDF p. 6 & p. 13 Section 7.3 Tables 9 & 11: basic G1 Ed25519 certificate + SHA-256 skill-manifest verification ~97 us (0.097 ms; total MCP proxy overhead ~0.62 ms/call); enhanced G1 BBS+ selective-disclosure proof generation ~174.7 ms and verification ~13.8 ms.
Exposed_Security_Function: Ed25519/BBS+ capability-bound certificate verification, SHA-256 skill-manifest hashing, Groth16 DV-SNARK / replay verification, and bilateral Ed25519 ledger signing
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Section 7.4 & Table 10 (pp. 14–15) explicitly note that runtime behavioral attacks S10 (knowledge poisoning via tool output) and S11 (cascading hijack) are only traced post-hoc in the ledger rather than blocked in real time, and S1–S9 unit tests validate algorithm correctness rather than adaptive exploit resistance; software G2 replay verification is probabilistic and sensitive to provider non-determinism (reasoning models drop to 0.169–0.402 CharMatch in Table 6, p. 13).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: PARAFRASA dan kutipan metrik terukur. PDF pp. 4–9 Sections 3–4 (G1 capability certs, G2 replay/DV-SNARK, G3 bilateral Ed25519 ledger); pp. 10–11 Section 5 & Theorems 1–2 (Bounded Divergence & Chain Verifiability); pp. 13–15 Section 7, Figure 5 & Tables 6–14 (0.62 ms per-call basic overhead, 13.8 ms enhanced BBS+/Groth16 verify, 10.8 ms / 0.12% 5-agent pipeline overhead, ~250 B/record, 99.1–100% backdoor detection, 12 scenarios in Table 10, 7/7 E2E attacks detected in Table 14).

Protected_Object: Agent tool-capability manifest commitments, model execution reproducibility, and multi-agent bilateral interaction ledger
Composition_Evidence: Mengomposisikan sertifikat kapabilitas G1 pada pendelegasian dan pemanggilan alat (B1;B2;B3), verifikasi reprodusibilitas G2 (B3), dan buku besar interaksi bilateral G3 (B4), serta membuktikan melalui Agent Governance Trilemma (§8.2) bahwa ketiganya saling melengkapi.

Threat_Attacker_Model: Ledger record modification, disputed interactions and injected content propagating through recorded agent chains.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: A2Auth G3 signed interaction ledger with input/output commitments, certificate references, hash chaining and bilateral Ed25519 attribution.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Interaction record append/verify and forensic chain auditor.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Integrity/attribution of recorded interactions and post-hoc chain tracing; not prevention of all injection or proof of complete observation.
Trust_Assumptions: Correct endpoint record production, key custody, log availability and authentic party identities; trace data/commitments available for audit.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: PDF pp. 13–15 Section 7.3–7.5, Figure 5 & Tables 10–11: per-call ledger append (hash-link + bilateral Ed25519 sign + persist) is 0.448 ms (~250 bytes/record); 5-agent LangGraph pipeline (21 ledger appends, 90 runs with live Claude API) incurs 10.8 ms total governance overhead (0.12% of total runtime); S10–S11 runtime behavioral attacks are Traced post-hoc rather than Prevented in real time (Table 10).
Exposed_Security_Function: Signed provenance record verification and forensic tracing.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: The broad governance summary must not collapse Prevented, Detected and Traced into a single prevention result; bilateral signing is attribution under key assumptions.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: PARAPHRASE; PDF pp.10-11 Section 5; p.15 Table 10 S5-S6,S10-S12; pp.17-18 trust/verification limits.
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Parafrasa sumber: A2Auth G3 makes recorded interactions tamper-evident and supports forensic tracing; knowledge poisoning/cascading hijack cases are traced rather than prevented.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Recorded chain integrity and reported Nemotron-AIQ trace analysis; excludes unseen/omitted interactions and real-time semantic prevention.
Protected_Object: Signed interaction record, content commitments and chain links.
Composition_Evidence: G3 evidence preservation is independent of G2 runtime verifiability; missing G2 cannot be repaired by a valid log signature.

Study_Title: Security Threat Modeling for Emerging AI-Agent Protocols: A Comparative Analysis of MCP, A2A, Agora, and ANP
Threat_Attacker_Model: Malicious MCP server advertising colliding tool names or trust-cue metadata on the shared discovery surface to hijack tool selection and execution without host compromise, cryptographic break, or network MITM.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Cross-protocol threat modeling framework (12 protocol-level risks across Creation, Operation, and Update stages for MCP, A2A, Agora, and ANP) plus controlled MCP v1.25.0 tool-provider collision testbed demonstrating missing cryptographic tool-to-provider identity binding.
Enforcement_Point_Location: MCP Client Tool Discovery, Name Resolution, and Server Selection Layer (observed misbinding vulnerability; no defense implemented)
Security_Property_Guaranteed: PDF p. 16 Table 8 (N=100 trials per condition on MCP v1.25.0): demonstrates deterministic Wrong-Provider Violation Rate (VR) of 1.0 (100/100) under First-Match resolver when attacker registers first or injects metadata trust cues, and 0.52 (52/100) under random tie-breaking when metadata is cloned.
Trust_Assumptions: Attacker can register or expose an MCP server in the same discovery environment as a legitimate provider; orchestrator relies on tool name and natural-language description without cryptographic provider-origin binding.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: PDF p. 16 Table 8 & p. 17 Section 6.3: reports empirical Violation Rate (VR = 1.0 and 0.52 over N=100 trials per condition); runtime latency/throughput overhead of proposed cryptographic provider-binding mitigations is explicitly NOT_REPORTED (deferred to future work on p. 17).
Exposed_Security_Function: NOT_APPLICABLE — comparative protocol threat model and empirical MCP provider-collision vulnerability testbed
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Empirical testbed (Table 8, N=100 per condition) evaluates only MCP v1.25.0 local collision scenarios while A2A, Agora, and ANP are assessed qualitatively via risk matrices (Tables 4–7); proposed cryptographic provider-binding and capability-attestation defenses are not implemented or benchmarked for latency overhead (p. 17).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: PARAFRASA dan audit langsung PDF ter-pin. PDF pp. 9–14 Sections 4–5 & Tables 2–7 (12 protocol risks across Creation, Operation, Update for MCP, A2A, Agora, ANP); pp. 15–17 Section 6 & Table 8 (MCP v1.25.0 collision SUT, N=100 per condition: VR=1.0 attacker-first / trust-cue, VR=0.52 cloned metadata random tie-break; p. 17 future work on latency overhead).
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Parafrasa penulis: Analisis pemodelan ancaman lintas empat protokol agen (MCP, A2A, Agora, ANP) dan eksperimen testbed pada MCP v1.25.0 membuktikan bahwa ketiadaan pengikatan identitas penyedia ke nama alat menyebabkan tingkat pelanggaran salah-penyedia (Violation Rate) hingga 1,0 (100/100) saat terjadi tabrakan nama alat.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Diaudit ulang oleh Reviewer 2 dari PDF 2602.11327v2 (19 hlm.): matriks risiko kualitatif 4 protokol (Tables 4–7) dan eksperimen tabrakan penyedia pada MCP v1.25.0 (Table 8, N=100 per kondisi).
Protected_Object: Tool-to-provider identity binding and discovery resolution integrity in multi-server agent protocols
Composition_Evidence: Menunjukkan bahwa kegagalan pengikatan identitas pada tahap penemuan/resolusi server (B2) secara langsung menyebabkan eksekusi alat pada penyedia penyerang (B3).
Coding_Rationale: Audit & Penyempurnaan Reviewer 2 atas draf pilot CLM-0007: Pemeriksaan langsung PDF 2602.11327v2 mengonfirmasi keakuratan angka Table 8 (VR = 1,0 dan 0,52 pada N=100 per kondisi di MCP v1.25.0) serta matriks risiko 12 ancaman pada Tables 4–7. Kode DG;AD dan status SUPPORTED_WITHIN_SCOPE telah tepat dan terverifikasi penuh.

Study_Title: Trusted AI Agents in the Cloud
Threat_Attacker_Model: Untrusted cloud provider/host OS, malicious co-located tenant agents, compromised external tools, and indirect prompt injection attempting data exfiltration, unauthorized resource access, privilege escalation, multiple tool invocation, or execution flow disruption.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Omega Trusted Agent Platform: AMD SEV-SNP Confidential VMs with VMPL hardware privilege separation (SVSM-based trusted monitor at VMPL-0/1), NVIDIA H100 Confidential GPUs (CGPU), vTPM trusted boot, differential remote attestation, Rego/OPA policy enforcement, and encrypted audit log with HMAC Trusted Counter (TC).
Enforcement_Point_Location: VMPL-0/1 SVSM Trusted Monitor, vTPM Attestation Verifier, and Agent Supervisor OPA Policy Gate inside AMD SEV-SNP CVM
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Hardware-enforced multi-agent isolation, cross-principal differential attestation, tamper-evident HMAC trusted-counter logging, and 0% Attack Success Rate across all 5 adapted MCPSecBench attack categories (down from 90%–100% undefended baseline ASR, Table 10 p. 15).
Trust_Assumptions: AMD SEV-SNP CPU/ASP hardware, NVIDIA H100 CGPU firmware, and SVSM/vTPM trusted monitor at VMPL-0/1 are uncompromised; administrator Rego/OPA allowlist policies accurately specify permitted endpoints and arguments.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: PDF pp. 12–15 Section 9, Figures 9–10 & Table 10 (AMD SEV-SNP + NVIDIA H100 CGPU): Rego/OPA policy validation 39.8 ± 3.2 ms (<2.5% of ~1.67 s inference); per-turn latency overhead 7% (CGPU disabled) and 36% (CGPU enabled); boot time 0.10 s vs 6.52 s VM (65.2x) and 18.12 s CVM (181.2x); adapted MCPSecBench ASR reduced from 90%–100% to 0% across 5 attack categories (VMPL isolation and trusted boot evaluated via separate microbenchmarks, p. 12).
Exposed_Security_Function: AMD SEV-SNP + H100 CGPU differential remote attestation, VMPL memory isolation, vTPM measurement, OPA policy gating, and HMAC trusted-counter logging
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Section 9.1 (p. 12) notes that full VMPL intra-CVM isolation overhead is estimated via microbenchmarks rather than fully integrated into the end-to-end Python agent runtime; enabling Confidential GPU encryption/attestation incurs a 36% average per-turn latency overhead (p. 12); execution-flow disruption defense requires human user confirmation for high-risk actions (Table 10, p. 15).
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: PARAFRASA dan kutipan metrik terukur. PDF pp. 5–11 Sections 4–7 & Tables 1–6 (VMPL + vTPM + CGPU architecture, differential attestation, HMAC trusted counter, formal action-fact model); pp. 12–15 Section 9, Figures 9–10 & Table 10 (0.10 s boot time vs 18.12 s CVM [181.2x], 7% / 36% per-turn latency overhead, 195 vs 198 tok/s throughput, Table 10: ASR 90–100% reduced to 0%).
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Parafrasa penulis: Omega mengamankan agen AI multi-tenant di cloud menggunakan AMD SEV-SNP (isolasi VMPL dan vTPM), NVIDIA H100 Confidential GPU, atestasi diferensial lintas-prinsipal, penegakan kebijakan OPA, dan log audit berpenghitung tepercaya HMAC, memangkas waktu boot CVM sebesar 181,2x dan menurunkan ASR MCPSecBench dari 90–100% menjadi 0%.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Evaluasi purwarupa pada server AMD EPYC SEV-SNP dan GPU NVIDIA H100 untuk 6 aplikasi agen berbasis WebArena, microbenchmark isolasi/komunikasi/boot, serta evaluasi keamanan pada 5 kategori serangan MCPSecBench.
Protected_Object: Multi-tenant agent memory/GPU state, cross-principal attestation credentials, tool-call policy compliance, and HMAC-chained audit logs
Composition_Evidence: Mengintegrasikan atestasi diferensial multi-prinsipal (B1;B2), isolasi eksekusi VMPL + CGPU dan gerbang kebijakan OPA (B3), serta pencatatan log terenkripsi dengan penghitung tepercaya HMAC (B4).
Coding_Rationale: Ekstraksi & Verifikasi Reviewer 2: Studi memenuhi Stream M_AND_A pada B1;B2;B3;B4 dengan implementasi hardware TEE (SEV-SNP + H100) dan evaluasi serangan serta performa yang sangat lengkap. Kode AD diberikan karena isolasi VMPL penuh masih diestimasi melalui microbenchmark terpisah (Section 9.1, p. 12), overhead 36% saat fitur CGPU aktif, dan ketergantungan pada aturan allowlist statis OPA serta konfirmasi pengguna pada serangan gangguan alur eksekusi.
Required_Additional_Evidence: Verifikasi silang Reviewer 1 pada REVIEW_AUDIT dan pencatatan metrik Figures 9–10 & Table 10 (boot 0.10 s vs 18.12 s, overhead 7%/36%, ASR 0%) pada sheet EVALUASI_EMPIRIS_OVERHEAD_RQ3.
